translation_notes: Both g.query(text, initBindings={...}) calls bind a variable (paper, sent) that is NOT in the query's own SELECT list, so per the bind_initbindings row of the correspondence table each becomes a term interpolation ({rdflib.URIRef(PAPER)}, {rdflib.URIRef(sent)}) in the s{ } query text, in place of the corresponding ?paper / ?sent occurrences, rather than a call-suffix s{ }(bindings=...).

Test harness restored (kind=function, module-level helper call, see original.py): _seed_ttl() in the real file reads datasets/papers/seed/paper.ttl (521 KB) from disk; redefined here to read fixture.ttl instead, identically on both sides -- same on-disk-fixture rename already used for examples/trav_single_value/BD2KOnFHIR__fhirtordf__.../test_value. demo() turns a failed assertion into a comparable value instead of letting run_pair abort on the first raise, same convention as that example.

fixture.ttl is hand-authored (not a trimmed real file, unlike the FHIR precedent): two complete paper->sec->para->sent chains so LIMIT 1 has more than one candidate, plus a linked-but-untyped para (must not satisfy '?para a doco:Paragraph') and a second paper's own complete chain (must not surface once ?paper is interpolated as the exact PAPER IRI) as the neighbourhood that must not match.

No genuine zero-solution fixture: test_structure_round_trip() asserts non-emptiness of both `down` and `up`, so a fixture engineered to miss would make BOTH sides raise the same AssertionError and demo() catch it identically on both -- a green for the wrong reason. The zero-solution requirement is met instead by the neighbourhood triples above, which the query must skip while still finding a match elsewhere.

repair.driver: Seam: demo(fixture=...) sets the file _seed_ttl() reads (identical harness edit in original.py and translated.ldpy, region body untouched); 12 new fixtures, one call each, each making one pattern decisive whatever the store order: only another paper has a chain (zero solutions for PAPER), sec/para/sent typed otherwise, each po:contains link of the down path replaced by another predicate, up-links on another sentence only, no wasQuotedFrom, no referenceContext, wrong context, and decoys written before the real chain for the up-query patterns only an order can expose.
mutants_killed: po:contains -> variable predicate in each of the three down links
repair.remaining: LIMIT 1 removed from both queries stays green: the test reads only down[0] and up[0], so the mutant is not observable (the translation keeps LIMIT 1 verbatim). Two up-query kills rely on the store yielding the decoys first (no ORDER BY in the original).
